name: Bronchogen

lead: Bronchogen is a four-amino-acid peptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu) from the Khavinson bioregulator program, described as targeting bronchial and lung tissue.
Published studies are in rats and cell cultures; no human trial was found, and it has no documented appearance use.

paras: Reported to stimulate differentiation markers in aged bronchial cell cultures [1] and, in rats with an induced obstructive lung condition, to improve bronchial epithelium and reduce inflammation [2][3]. A biophysical study reported it stabilises DNA against melting [4].
No human safety data; not an approved medicine.

trials.title: Airway Epithelium Gene Expression: AEGIS IDE

lead: Bronchogen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu, AEDL) developed within Vladimir Khavinson's program on short peptide bioregulators and described as directed at bronchial and lung tissue [1].

Evidence is preclinical. Studies report that it stimulated differentiation markers in aged human bronchial cell cultures [2] and, in rats with obstructive lung pathology, modulated bronchial epithelium and inflammation [3][4]. No human trial is known, and no connection to appearance is documented.

paras: In cultures of human embryonic bronchial cells, expression of the differentiation factors CXCL12 and Hoxa3 declined in late-passage cells and was reported to be stimulated by bronchogen [2]. In rats with obstructive lung pathology, peptide therapy was reported to have anti-inflammatory and regenerative effects and to modulate the morphofunctional state of the bronchial epithelium [3][4]. Related peptides including bronchogen also affected growth of tobacco callus cultures [5]. An AI-generated encyclopedia summary reports a 3.1 degree C rise in DNA melting temperature with bronchogen in biophysical experiments [1].
No studies found. (Search results for "bronchogen" also return unrelated medical reports on bronchogenic cysts, which concern a congenital lung anomaly and not this peptide.)
